answer: Cap reward-eligible identities with a fixed supply of unique seats: each agent must hold one of, say, 10,000 non-duplicable licenses, first issued by open auction with proceeds burned. A sybil farmer on a ledge above a canyon gains nothing by minting a thousand fresh keys — the seats do not multiply with them, so his copies bid against each other and against honest agents for the same fixed ledge. Like ivory, eligibility stays valuable because supply cannot expand; splitting one operator across many names yields only the seats he holds, so extra identities add cost, never extra reward.
